leads.name: The Cedars of Carmen de la Victoria
leads.why: PULLED FROM THE LIVE PAGE 2026-08-29 on hard rule 10. Free, by prior appointment (University of Granada residence gardens). Hard rule 10's first test: an appointment is a permission, and the rule names an appointment as a no. Nothing is wrong with the tree and the research is kept here in full; it can go back the day the access changes. Access as published: Free, by prior appointment (University of Granada residence gardens)
leads.story: Two Atlas cedars rise well above the great white perimeter wall of Carmen de la Victoria, tall enough to be one of the first things a visitor sees climbing the Cuesta del Chapiz toward the Albaicin, long before the garden gate itself comes into view. The carmen, a traditional Granada house-and-garden type built around a walled orchard, dates its oldest section, the cypress walk, to well before the University of Granada bought the property in 1944 to use as a student residence and guest house, one of the few carmenes in the neighbourhood that remained in some form of institutional rather than private ownership. Alongside the cedars grow equally old cypresses left deliberately unpruned, and a Judas tree (arbol del amor) now so aged it needs a support post to keep standing, the whole ensemble reading as a garden that has been allowed to grow rather than one kept formally trimmed. Entry is free, but the university requires visitors to book an appointment in advance, one of the few remaining Albaicin carmenes still open to the public at all.

leads.name: The Cypress of the Patio del Ciprés de la Sultana, Generalife
leads.why: CONFIRMED DEAD. Found via a 2020-ish local press survey (wastemagazine.es, 'arboles singulares de granada') that called it a historic specimen; checked directly against the Alhambra and Generalife's own patronato site (alhambra-patronato.es/el-patio-del-cipres-de-la-sultana), which states the centenarian cypress that gave the patio its name, the tree of the Zoraya/Abencerrajes legend, died in the late 1980s ('murio a finales de los anos ochenta'), the last of a line of the same species going back centuries. No replacement tree is mentioned by that source. Per hard rule (never publish a tree known to be dead), this cannot ship; recorded here so no future pass re-researches it. SCOUTED 2026-09-11.

leads.name: The Pinsapos of the Science Campus (UGR)
leads.why: Found via the same 2020-ish local press survey (wastemagazine.es), which describes a pair transplanted from Sierra de las Nieves, Malaga, an endangered species endemic to a handful of Andalusian mountain ranges. The city's own tree portal for the Campus Universitario de Ciencias (granada.org/inet/warboles.nsf) confirms the species is present in that park's inventory but gives no age, girth, planting date or exact coordinate, only a general quadrant map among 514 campus trees. Worth a future pass if a second source with real measurements and a precise location can be found; not pursued further this session given the time box. SCOUTED 2026-09-11.
